move: donut ring fills in two segments with counters, unwinds for the loop
how: A white dashboard card holds a 300px SVG donut and a three-row legend. From 4% the dark blue segment grows to 58% of the ring (stroke-dasharray driven by an expo.out proxy tween over 1.6s) and from 30% a lighter segment extends behind it to 80%; the centre percentage and the three dollar values are recomputed in the same onUpdate. The donut pops from scale .96 to 1.02 with back.out(3) and settles; legend rows slide in from x 30 with a 0.12s stagger. At 80% the segments unwind (p2 then p1, power3.in / expo.inOut) and the rows slide out reversed, with a set() at the last frame restoring them so frame 0 matches.
adapt: Change the two percentages, the money format and total (1.2M), the legend labels, title and the two blues; keep the expo.out 1.6s fill and the unwind timing.
port: mount(el, shot) builds the card, SVG and legend from shot.segments; animate returns the timeline with the fills at 0.04D and 0.3D and the unwind at 0.8D. The draw() closure must query its elements inside el; the final set() at D-0.001 is what closes the loop, keep it.
caveats: from() tweens need immediateRender:false when composed into a larger timeline
